(3) As Little AI As Possible

  • The line between AI and deterministic code keeps moving
  • Good architecture is what lets you move it
  • All of it rests on foundations this talk mostly takes for granted


Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(4) A Trillion Operations for 16'968 ÷ 404?

CPU Computation LLM Inference
Elapsed time a few nanoseconds ~0.1–2 seconds
Computation one integer division ~1011–1013 FLOPs
Energy ~pJ–nJ ~1–100 J
Correctness exact not guaranteed
  • CPU: One deterministic instruction
  • LLM: Trillions of operations for probabilistic inference
  • The LLM might still get the answer wrong


Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(5) Before AI

  • Code runs deterministically


Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(6) Machine Learning (ML): 2010s

  • Training models for specific problems becomes mainstream, but it is costly
  • One model per problem does not scale


Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(7) GenAI: 2022

  • LLMs make ML more widely applicable and much cheaper, but they are isolated
  • Powerful, but hard to make work in a predictable way


Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(8) Prompt Engineering: 2023

  • First attempts to better manage probabilistic LLMs
  • Better instructions, but still no eyes or hands


Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(9) Function Calling: June 2023

  • LLMs are not just a brain in a jar anymore
  • One model to rule them all is not the best approach


Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(10) Subagents: 2024

  • Decomposing problems into sub-problems for specific contexts or models
  • Models need to have a standardized way to reach out into the world


Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(11) Model Context Protocol: November 2024

  • Interact directly with context in a standardized way
  • Using tools is useful but finding the right ones is hard


Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(12) Agent Skills: October 2025

  • Prepackaged mixes of prompts, local tools, and external tools
  • Some questions should be decided before models start their work


Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(13) Decision Models (RLCD): September 2026

  • Move from human-friendly LLMs to machine-friendly structured output
  • Some decisions can be followed by prescribed processes


Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(14) Workflows

  • Turn repeated processes into repeatable, reliable, reviewable, discoverable workflows
  • Once processes are stable, they can become part of the foundation


Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(15) Everything Everywhere All at Once

  • Expect this menagerie to change at a rapid clip


Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(16) Solution Architecture Is Only Part of It

  • All of these mechanisms are about composing a solution
  • Every one of them has to interact with APIs and data
  • Wiring that up is where many AI efforts stall or don't scale
  • AI integration architecture matters as much as AI solution architecture


Erik Wilde: Composable Architecture for AI Systems: APIs, MCP, Skills, Sub-Agents, and Workflows

(17) Monday Tasks

  • Keep watching what arrives, because the line will move again
  • Modularize by subproblem, so that you can move the line later
  • Invest in the APIs and data that everything else has to reach
